In general, aliphatic saturated hydrocarbons, also known as alkanes, are gases at lower molecular weights, become liquids as their molecular weight increases, and eventually become solids at even higher molecular weights. This is due to the increasing strength of van der Waals forces as the molecular size and surface area increase.
